Well, "working against me" makes it sound like I think there's some kind of cinematic conspiracy with people in dark rooms plotting my downfall, and that's not what I'm saying at all. I'm a logical person, doctor. I deal in facts. But what I am saying is that human behavior, when you couple it with digital evidence, creates a very clear, undeniable pattern that you simply cannot ignore. 

Like I was saying before, I know everyone—my sister, the estate lawyers, the rest of my family—they keep telling me the hospital records and those charity donation emails all line up perfectly. They just look at the surface-level PDF exports, they see the letterhead, and they say, "Yep, it's all fine, let's move on." But when I actually get into the metadata, when I sit down and compare the precise timestamps on the email headers—down to the millisecond—and cross-reference them with the hospital's admission and discharge logs, there are glaring discrepancies. And it's not just a system glitch. There are missing attachments. There are these sequential gaps in the file naming conventions. You don't just skip from file 'DOC_4092' to 'DOC_4099' in an automated medical or legal system unless someone manually intervened and scrubbed the files in between. That requires administrative access and intent. 

And then, you look at the real-world reactions. I take this data, right? I go to certain community members, people who were supposedly his best friends, people heavily involved with his charity, and I just ask for basic clarification. I say, "Hey, can you explain this routing gap on the night of the 14th?" And suddenly, their whole demeanor changes. They won't look me in the eye. They physically turn away, they make up flimsy excuses about being late to pick up their kids, or they just completely stop returning my texts and calls altogether. 

So, you ask if I believe they're hiding something? It’s absolutely obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. The data doesn't lie, and their physical avoidance just confirms what the data is already screaming at me. I just don't understand why I'm the only one willing to look at the raw numbers. It’s like everyone else is just choosing to be blind, and I'm left holding all this evidence that proves the official story is a fabrication.

It’s just... it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. You don't get a perfect storm of digital anomalies and synchronized evasive behavior by accident. It just doesn't happen. The probability is practically zero. So, no, I don't think there's a simpler explanation. I think the simplest explanation is the one the data is pointing to, which is that the official story is flawed, and people are actively choosing not to address it.

Responsibility? Yeah... yeah, I mean, it’s more than just a responsibility, doctor, it’s... it’s a weight. It’s this massive, crushing weight that I wake up with every single morning. So, yes, I feel a profound personal responsibility. I feel like I owe it to my dad to not just let his final days be... be rewritten by some sanitized, fabricated paper trail. I'm his son. I don't have a choice, no matter how much people want me to just drop it.

Consider the possibility? I mean... look, if this were just a matter of, you know, a few missing puzzle pieces, maybe. If it was just a case of "we don't know exactly what time the nurse checked on him" or "we don't have the final blood pressure reading," then sure. I could live with not having every single answer. I deal with incomplete data sets all the time in my line of work. Sometimes a log file gets corrupted, sometimes a user doesn't report an error properly... you learn to work around the gaps. You learn to accept a certain margin of error. 

But... and I know I keep coming back to this, doctor, I know I'm basically beating a dead horse here, but you really have to understand my position. It's not just that I don't have all the answers. It's that the answers they *are* giving me are structurally impossible. 

I know everyone keeps telling me—my sister, the lawyers, the estate executors, literally everyone—they all keep saying the hospital records and those charity donation emails all line up perfectly. They want it to be this neat little package so they can just put a bow on it and walk away. But I'm the one actually looking under the hood. And when I sit there and compare the timestamps, down to the exact second, and I look at those missing attachments that nobody will even acknowledge exist, and then... then I go out and see the way certain community members completely shut down and physically avoid my questions about those exact discrepancies... I mean, I can't just "consider the possibility" that the official report is true. It defies basic logic. 

It's not about lacking answers, it's about the presence of active manipulation. It’s just so incredibly obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. So to answer your question... no. I can't just accept the reported version, because the reported version is a fabrication. It's a bad patch over a glaring system error, and I can't just pretend the system is running fine when I can see the code is completely broken.

I mean... feelings? No. No, absolutely not, doctor. If anything, it's the exact opposite. Look, I’m a systems analyst, right?
